items.title: 1Password Security Incident
items.summary: A 1Password employee's GitHub account was compromised, allowing an attacker to push malicious code that exfiltrated limited customer metadata. No vault contents were accessed, but the breach highlights supply‑chain risk.
items.why_it_matters: Directly impacts credential‑management tooling that many engineers rely on; requires immediate security hygiene.
items.next_step_detail: Review the incident report and rotate any 1Password credentials or API tokens used in CI/CD pipelines.

items.title: A tool call cut at "append":tru came back as valid JSON, without append
items.summary: Report of a bug in jiter 0.18.0 used by Anthropic's Python SDK where truncated tool calls produce malformed JSON, causing silent data loss.
items.why_it_matters: A breaking issue in a library many production agents rely on; needs immediate patch to avoid corrupted tool executions.
items.next_step_detail: Upgrade jiter to >=0.19.0 (pip install --upgrade jiter) or pin Anthropic SDK to a version that bundles the fix.

items.title: Nfs2root: A 12-year-old pre-auth remote root in the Linux kernel's NFS server
items.summary: A pre‑authentication heap overflow in the Linux NFS server (nfsd) allows remote code execution, fixed in recent kernel releases. The advisory provides CVE‑2026‑99362 details and upgrade instructions.
items.why_it_matters: If you run NFS services or Kubernetes storage nodes, the vulnerability can give attackers root access.
items.next_step_detail: Update to Linux 6.12.117 or later (e.g., `apt-get install linux-image-6.12.117 && reboot`).

items.title: Tracekit: a tamper-evident flight recorder for coding agents
items.summary: Introduces Tracekit, a signed hash‑chain logger that records every tool call of a coding agent, making logs tamper‑evident and verifiable.
items.why_it_matters: Provides essential security and auditability for autonomous agents operating in production environments.
items.next_step_detail: Run `pip install tracekit && tracekit init` and integrate the provided hooks into your agent framework.

items.title: Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT
items.summary: AutoGPT is an open‑source Python framework that lets developers create autonomous AI agents capable of planning, executing, and iterating on tasks without human intervention.
items.why_it_matters: Core building block for production‑grade autonomous workflows; widely adopted and actively maintained.
items.next_step_detail: Run `pip install autogpt && autogpt --help` to explore its CLI and sample agents.

items.title: mvanhorn / last30days-skill
items.summary: A Python skill for AI agents that crawls Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket, and the web to produce a grounded summary of a topic. It can be plugged into multi‑agent workflows.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a ready‑to‑use research skill that accelerates building autonomous agents with up‑to‑date web knowledge.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the example script to see the summarization output.

items.title: ArXiv: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
items.summary: Study introduces Delta Residue Attribution to measure and explain unnecessary edits made by coding agents compared to human developers.
items.why_it_matters: Directly informs how to evaluate and improve the efficiency of autonomous coding agents you may deploy.
items.next_step_detail: Read the paper and consider applying DRA metrics to your own agent pipelines.

items.title: Can Your Agent Review Your Cloud Architecture?
items.summary: Describes the AWS Agent Toolkit that runs a Well‑Architected review skill, reading code and AWS docs to generate an evidence‑backed architecture report.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a concrete multi‑agent workflow that can automate cloud‑architecture compliance checks for staff engineers.
items.next_step_detail: Install the Agent Toolkit via `pip install aws-agent-toolkit` and run `aws-well-architected-review .` on a test repo.

items.title: AI model failover that never failed back: 17 days on a local model
items.summary: A post‑mortem of an OpenRouter outage where four AI agents were switched to a local LLM and operated uninterrupted for 17 days.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a practical failover pattern for resilient agent deployments using local models.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article to understand the switch‑over script and replication setup.

items.title: Stop AI Agents Acting on Bluffs? A Strands Decider 2B Tool Gate Test
items.summary: The author evaluates Strands Decider 2B as a gate for AI agents on 16 refund cases, measuring accuracy, latency, cost and robustness to prompt injection.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete assessment of a tool‑gate that can protect production agents from malicious or noisy inputs.
items.next_step_detail: Read the full article to understand the evaluation methodology and results.

items.title: ArXiv: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
items.summary: Study shows that using certain attack policies to evaluate AI monitors can produce misleading safety metrics, demonstrated on an OpenAI monitor.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights a pitfall in safety evaluation pipelines that engineers must account for when deploying monitors for agents.
items.next_step_detail: Read the paper to adjust your monitor evaluation strategy.

items.title: Predicting LoRA size for any dataset
items.summary: The blog post proposes a method to estimate the optimal LoRA rank for a given dataset, balancing performance and parameter efficiency. It includes empirical formulas and guidance for large‑scale fine‑tuning.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a practical way to size LoRA adapters, reducing trial‑and‑error when customizing open‑source LLMs.
items.next_step_detail: Apply the suggested formula to your next LoRA fine‑tuning run and compare results.

items.title: HF Paper: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
items.summary: Introduces OWE‑Bench, a 26‑task benchmark covering software, physical, ML, and scientific engineering challenges for long‑horizon agents.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete evaluation suite for the multi‑step agent workflows you build.
items.next_step_detail: Compare OWE‑Bench to any internal benchmarks you use for agent performance.

items.title: Jev is probably Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
items.summary: Discussion analyzing latency measurements to infer that the Jev model is likely Qwen3.5‑35B‑A3B.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a practical method for identifying hidden model versions, useful when selecting local LLMs for agents.
items.next_step_detail: Read the blog post to learn the latency‑profiling technique.

items.title: Inside APIC: The Full Engineering Teardown of a Free Photo Editor & Background Remover That Runs 100% On Your Device
items.summary: A deep dive into APIC, a browser‑based photo editor that runs AI models locally after a one‑time download, avoiding server uploads.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates techniques for local model loading and privacy‑preserving inference that can be applied to on‑device LLM workflows.
items.next_step_detail: Study the implementation details to adapt local model caching for your own Python services.

items.title: I checked Clojure's core with Lean and found unreported bugs
items.summary: The author used Lean 4 to formally verify parts of Clojure's core libraries and discovered several bugs that were not previously reported.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a practical method for finding supply‑chain vulnerabilities in language runtimes that could affect Python or other stacks.
items.next_step_detail: Read the blog post to understand the verification workflow and consider applying similar checks to critical Python packages.

items.title: Bare Metal Qwen
items.summary: A GitHub repository demonstrating how to run the Qwen LLM directly on bare‑metal hardware using assembly and minimal OS components. It showcases low‑level model execution techniques.
items.why_it_matters: Shows possibilities for ultra‑lightweight LLM deployment on constrained devices.

items.title: A security audit found 11 issues. Five of my fixes had bugs of their own.
items.summary: The author recounts a security audit of the open‑source Shipkeep platform, noting that several attempted fixes introduced new bugs.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights the importance of thorough testing after security patches, relevant for maintaining AI agent deployment pipelines.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article to learn the audit findings and apply similar validation steps to your own infra.

items.title: Your README lies. I built a tool that proves it with Kane CLI
items.summary: The author created Kane CLI, a tool that checks whether a project's README matches its actual behavior, exposing drift between documentation and code.
items.why_it_matters: Helps maintain accurate docs for AI agent projects and prevents hidden mismatches in deployment scripts.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `kane verify .` on a Python project.

items.title: ArXiv: μ-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.summary: Presents μ‑Bench, a benchmark for evaluating voice agents that must handle concurrent multi‑user requests while respecting privacy and authority constraints.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a testing framework that could be adapted to evaluate multi‑agent coordination in text‑based AI assistants.
items.next_step_detail: Download the benchmark suite and skim the evaluation metrics.

items.title: affaan-m/ECC
items.summary: ECC is a JavaScript framework that adds performance‑optimizing agents with skills, memory, and security layers for LLMs like Claude and Codex. It targets code‑centric workflows and browser‑based agents.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a novel way to embed security and memory into LLM‑driven agents, which can inspire similar Python implementations.
items.next_step_detail: Browse the repo to understand its architecture and consider porting useful patterns to Python.

items.title: SSH is a GUI framework
items.summary: Article demonstrates using SSH’s extended terminal capabilities to render graphical interfaces, including a microVM desktop over SSH.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a low‑overhead way to expose UI for remote agents without additional tooling.
items.next_step_detail: Review the implementation details to see if it fits your remote‑agent UI needs.

items.title: HF Paper: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
items.summary: Proposes a conditional pretraining approach that builds steerability into language models from the ground up, reducing reliance on post‑hoc alignment.
items.why_it_matters: Relevant for building agents whose behavior can be safely constrained via built‑in conditioning.
items.next_step_detail: Read the paper to assess if the conditioning method fits your agent control stack.

items.title: ArXiv: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
items.summary: The paper surveys privacy, security, and ethical challenges when deploying LLMs in telecommunications services. It outlines threat vectors, data leakage risks, and regulatory considerations.
items.why_it_matters: Helps engineers anticipate compliance and safety issues when integrating LLMs into telecom‑related workflows.

items.title: HF Paper: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
